_comment: Machine-readable voice registry for the TMB audio pipeline. This file holds ONLY the
machine fields a script needs. The prose canon for each character stays in
story-rules/CHARACTERS.md, which points here for voice data, so voice IDs live in
ElevenLabs VOICE IDs are NOT secrets and belong in this repository.
The ElevenLabs API KEY is a secret and must never appear in any file here.
A speaker with elevenLabsVoiceId null is UNASSIGNED. Validation reports it and
generation refuses to run for it. Never invent a voice ID.
voiceVersion: bump this when a character's voice is re-cast or re-tuned in a way that
should invalidate their cached audio. It is part of the cache fingerprint, so bumping it
regenerates that character's clips and nobody else's.

pronouns: used by the parser to resolve an actor like "He reached for the intercom." to a speaker. Resolution always picks the most recently NAMED character with that pronoun, and the attribution method is recorded as pronoun-actor so a reviewer can spot-check it.

narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.notes: Audiobook only. Not exported to the game dialogue manifest.

system.name: TOMBS / settlement systems
system.notes: Machine readouts. Spoken in the audiobook and reusable in the game.

lena-ortiz.name: Lena Ortiz
lena-ortiz.notes: Heard only through a wrist-terminal call. A filtered/radio treatment may suit her.

doctor-mercer.name: Doctor Mercer
doctor-mercer.notes: Introduced in Chapter 4 of the revised manuscript. Runs the medical center overnight; heard only through Jack's wrist terminal. Sarah's 'I like her' makes the character she/her. Voice assigned by Joshua on 2026-09-21.

security-officer.name: Settlement security
security-officer.notes: ONE VOICE FOR THE SETTLEMENT'S SECURITY OFFICERS, assigned by Joshua on 2026-09-21. On 2026-09-22 his revised Chapter 5 named the officer who drives Jack to the boundary: Mark Jones, perimeter security, who then has some thirty lines across Chapters 5 and 6 and is a returning character. 'Mark', 'Mark Jones' and 'Jones' are aliases of this speaker so the parser reads his beats. Chapter 4's Unit Twelve, a man's voice on the south-patrol channel, is read in the same voice; the manuscript does not say whether he is Mark. If a second, distinct officer ever speaks, split this into named speakers -- after generation that costs clips.
